Load

title: Green Book Section I.C.1.a Measurability
text:
Discussion


Scope — what I.C.1.a measures (optional)

This page answers only whether perennial vegetation change is measurable vs the 1984–1987 baseline, parcel by parcel (Box I.C.1.a.ii). Measurable ≠ attributable ≠ significant.
Wellfield parcels with Cover_sig.counter > 5 or Grass_sig.counter > 5 appear in I.C.1.a flagged parcels for further analysis. The I.C.1.a flagged list identifies sustained measurable change; it does not establish causation. The “but for” question is evaluated using the factors described in attributability analysis. DTW and precipitation provide hydrologic screening context. NDVI is a vegetation index related to canopy greenness and chlorophyll; its relationship to water availability is conditional on which plants are present. These measures can reveal quality or co-variation, including checks for inflated or borrowed baselines. Not decided here: pooled wellfield/control averages as a Green Book test; causation (pumping vs drought, land use, surface-water practice, etc.).

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
This page explains how Green Book Section I.C.1.a measures vegetation decrease or change. It covers perennial cover, grass, and composition relative to each parcel’s 1984–1987 baseline. Causation (the “but for” question involving pumping or surface-water practice) belongs to I.C.1.b attributability analysis.
Authoritative checklist: config/measurability_procedure.yaml · Standing Committee box: GB memo 22 Feb 2017.

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
What the Box authorizes
Box I.C.1.a.ii states that statistical analysis for measurability may include, but is not limited to:







Domain
Methods




Cover
Welch t-test, Wilcox (Mann–Whitney), ANOVA, GLM; one-sample t when baseline transect n is small (e.g. 1–4)


Composition
PERMANOVA and NMDS



The Technical Group decides measurability case by case. Automation builds a preponderance table so every reinventory parcel can be screened the same way.

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
Cover suite








Method
Status
Role




Welch two-sample / one-sample t
Included
Provides the historical statistical counters for sustained cover or grass decreases; percentile context helps interpret the result


Wilcox / Mann–Whitney
Included
Rank-based comparison that provides an independent view of perennial cover and grass change


GLM (Gaussian)
Included
Model-based comparison of current observations with the baseline period


ANOVA
Included
Group comparison of baseline and current perennial cover or grass



What enters the decrease tests: perennial total cover and perennial grass — the groundwater-dependent layer the Agreement and Box were built around. A year counts toward the decrease counter when p < 0.05 and current mean is below baseline (same direction rule as the historical Welch path). That is a statistical pass/fail for I.C.1.a—not Agreement “significance” under I.C.1.c.

Annuals — diagnostic, not ignored
Line-point hits include annual species. Native and non-native annuals both can signal degraded or disturbed conditions (pulse after bare ground, weed invasion, loss of perennial structure). They are not dropped from the monitoring record.







Layer
Role




Perennial cover / grass / composition
Formal Box I.C.1.a decrease / change tests and counters


Annual_native / Annual_nonnative
Degradation context on timeseries and parcel cards



The parcel timeseries separates annual cover by provenance. These series provide visual context alongside perennial grass and shrub; formal annual response tests remain a possible future extension under the Box “may include” clause.

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
Percentile framing
For each parcel and metric (Cover, Grass, Shrub), the current year is scored as an empirical percentile within that parcel’s own full time series. Baseline years (1984–1987) are scored the same way so an inflated or atypical baseline is visible without treating Welch p < 0.05 as the whole story.







Output
Content




output/parcel_metric_percentiles_long.csv
Parcel × Year × metric percentiles


output/parcel_percentile_summary_flagged.csv
Current + baseline percentile summary for I.C.1.a flagged parcels



Percentiles keep each current value and baseline value on the same within-parcel scale, making unusual or inflated baselines easier to recognize.

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
Composition suite








Method
Status
Role




PERMANOVA (Bray–Curtis)
Live
Current-year transects vs 1985–87 baseline transects within the parcel


Dominant / indicator species
Included
Always shows the top five perennial cover dominants for baseline and current periods; statistically associated species may be appended as IndVal results (· IndVal: …)


NMDS / centroids
Live
Maps change in species composition through time; distances in species space make shifts and trajectories comparable. It informs the evidence picture but is not the sole I.C.1.a gate


Decade kernel / type space
Screening context
Identifies states outside a parcel’s historical Type A–E range; a composition state is not the same as its mapped Green Book type



Composition change can be measurable without a cover or grass decrease. NMDS places each parcel-year in species-composition space, so distances and trajectories show how the assemblage moves even when total cover does not. Those parcels appear in the evidence pack with change_type_label containing composition_shift or type_drift.

Dominant / indicator species (baseline and current)
For each reinventory parcel in 2026, the evidence-pack columns show the top five perennial cover dominants for that period, ranked by mean cover across transects (USDA PLANTS codes after ETL aliases):

indicator_species_baseline — top dominants in the 1984–87 sample
indicator_species_current — top dominants in the current year

IndVal is secondary. When indicspecies::multipatt (IndVal.g) finds significant baseline- or current-associates, they are appended as · IndVal: CODE; …. Empty IndVal no longer leaves dashes — dominants stay visible. Absence of IndVal associates does not mean “no change”; PERMANOVA can still reject no-change without a clean IndVal hit.


Ordination — headline species view
A short list of species accounts for most transect “top hits” (highest perennial cover on a transect). Across the LPT master, eight codes cover ~88% of transect-years as #1; twelve cover ~93%. Those codes are the headline palette in config/headline_species.yaml.

section: How to read the evidence pack
text:
How to read the evidence pack








Product
Rule
Meaning




Sustained decrease screen
Cover_sig.counter > 5 or Grass_sig.counter > 5 for a wellfield parcel
Highlights a persistent measurable decrease in perennial cover or grass


Evidence pack
Multiple methods applied to the monitoring year
Shows converging evidence, including composition-only change



The historical counters summarize sustained decreases, while the evidence pack adds independent tests and composition measures. Percentile framing places current and baseline values within each parcel’s own history, making baseline inflation and within-parcel rank visible. Together, the views show both cover-only and composition-only change.

title: Methods — Box I.C.1.a.ii evidence pack
text:
What is not attributability
NDVI is a vegetation index related to canopy greenness and chlorophyll. Precipitation and depth-to-water are separate hydrologic context. NDVI’s relationship to water availability is conditional on which plants are present, so NDVI is not itself hydrologic evidence. These measures do not decide I.C.1.b factors i–viii. Hydro-constrained CAP/SEM and “but for” modeling belong to attributability analysis (source).
